thread:
maria: Heads-up — after yesterday's VPC egress tightening rollout, several USW2 GPU nodes failed to complete keystore handshakes during onboarding. Seeing decrypt errors and long retries, warm-pool stayed empty. Sam: :eyes: saw the same in staging earlier, thought it was transient. Can you paste the error? maria: logs show KMS_DECRYPT_TIMEOUT and 403 from audit-shipper endpoint. Example: 
```
2026-03-22T14:03:12Z node-xyz keystore: decrypt err=KMS_DECRYPT_TIMEOUT attempt=3
2026-03-22T14:03:14Z node-xyz http: POST https://audit-shipper.internal/v1/logs -> 403 Forbidden
```
oliver: That 403 matches the new deny-by-default egress rule that only allows a few internal controlplane endpoints. audit-shipper's IPs are on the new allowlist but the keystore proxy uses a separate NAT egress path from the GPU subnets. zoe: so the control plane allowed the endpoint, but the worker egress path didn't. Nice catch. maria: Precisely — keystore proxy lives in the warm-pool subnet which gets an ephemeral natgw, and our new policy forgot to include the natgw's ENIs. Result: decryption falls back, node retries lots, GPU provisioning times out. sam: Impact: two batches of node joins failed in usw2 and our autoscaler rebalanced to other regions, increasing cross-region network egress and cost. Estimate ~+$2.3k/d in data transfer while warm-pool was starved. oliver: Short-term mitigation options: 1) revert egress deny for affected subnets, 2) add a targeted allow for keystore proxy nat ENIs, 3) route keystore traffic through controlplane egress. maria: Revert is easiest but policy owners want to avoid a full rollback. Proposal: add a narrow allowlist binding the specific NAT ENI IDs and keystore proxy SG to audit-shipper and kms endpoints for 2 hours. zoe: We can automate ENI discovery with a tiny lambda and apply the allow rule as a canary. keystore-bot: sched:apply-allowlist --target-subnet subnet-warm-02 --endpoints [kms.usw2.redwood-internal, audit-shipper.internal] --ttl 2h :white_check_mark: maria: If we do the lambda + allowlist, verify via the decrypt latency metric and node join success rate. Sam, can you run a quick canary? sam: spinning up 3 test nodes in warm-pool now. Will watch metric keystore.decrypt.latency and warm_pool.fill_time. oliver: Also watch KMS QPS, we saw a spike when nodes retried — that's a cost + throttling risk. Add alert if KMS 5xx rate > 1% for 5m. zoe: Long-term: we should consolidate keystore proxy egress through controlplane (single egress path) or use per-region static ENIs tied to role-bound NAT. That avoids edge-case allowlist misses. Also think about granting ephemeral session tokens scoped per-keystore-session to reduce retries on auth failures. maria: Agreed. I'll draft a short postmortem and a runbook: immediate canary (lambda + allowlist), 2h mitigation window, monitor, then follow-up RFC to change architecture (controlplane egress or static ENIs) and update firewall test matrix. sam: Canary result: 3/3 nodes joined, decrypt.latency dropped from median 1.8s -> 120ms, warm_pool.fill_time back to normal. KMS QPS spike flattened. maria: Good. I'm creating the temporary allowlist; tagging infra-policy for sign-off. oliver: For compliance, document the temporary exception (who approved, why, expiry) — security needs audit trail. Add the policy change to audit log retention 90d. zoe: I'll open the RFC with cost projections for static ENIs (est $1.6k/mo per region) vs continued mitigation overhead. maria: Thanks team. I'll post the postmortem + action items in #postmortems and close this thread when the RFC is merged. :thumbsup:
